title: The overview guide documents the success envelope without contractVersion, the key at index 1
description:
Surfaced by opum-agent 2026-09-18 while reporting a third instance of the absent-key-reads-as-null trap. Their instance was an ENVELOPE SHAPE error, not a nonexistent field: they ran quest task view <id> --json piped to jq selecting id, title, status and got a uniform null, because the record lives under .data and every key they named was absent at the top level. Exit 0, empty stderr, nothing indicating a shape mismatch. They nearly re-filed a task that existed, which on this tracker would have minted a duplicate id.

That prompted checking whether quest itself models a misleading idiom. It does not -- there are no jq examples anywhere in the guides or help. But the check found a real drift in the sentence that teaches the envelope.

THE DEFECT. src/application/agents/guides.ts line 67, in the OVERVIEW guide, states: Every command supports --json (the {schemaVersion, kind, data, principal} envelope). Measured against the built CLI: a success envelope is {schemaVersion, contractVersion, kind, data, principal} and an error envelope is {error_type, message, principal}. So the documented key list omits contractVersion, which QCLI-289 added and which the shared command contract fixes at index 1, and the single word "envelope" conceals that success and error are different shapes with no data key in common.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. This repositorys CLAUDE.md requires every agent to run quest instructions overview before answering or taking action, so this is the highest-traffic sentence quest ships and it is the sentence a caller reads immediately before writing a jq path. Handing someone an incomplete key list is the wrong input at exactly the moment they are constructing an accessor.

Not a contract change: the envelopes are correct, only their documentation is stale.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The overview guide names the success envelope keys exactly as the built CLI emits them, including contractVersion, verified by comparing the guide text against a real --json invocation rather than against the source
The guide distinguishes the success envelope from the error envelope rather than implying one shape, and says the record lives under data
A test pins the guide text against the actual envelope emitted by the CLI, so this specific drift is caught mechanically rather than by a reader noticing
The managed CLAUDE.md block is unaffected by the guide change, asserted with quest agents --check rather than assumed

implementationNotes:
THE TEST FOUND A SECOND DRIFT I WAS NOT LOOKING FOR, which is the main reason this task is worth more than its size. I set out to add the missing contractVersion. Asserting the guide against every key task list actually emits failed on "scope" -- DEC-6s additive key, which the guide also never mentioned. So the documented key list was short by TWO keys, not one, and the second was invisible to the inspection that found the first.

That changed the fix. An enumeration cannot stay complete against command-specific additive keys, so the guide now states the RULE instead: some commands add a key between data and principal (task list carries scope), principal is always last, and a caller must tolerate an unrecognized top-level key rather than treating the envelope as malformed. That last clause is the settled contract amendment, so the guide now teaches the tolerance the contract requires.

MUTATION PROOF, in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, because this test compares two artifacts and either could be the one that drifts. Predictions derived from reading the test file before running. M1, revert the guide to the pre-fix key list with the code untouched: predicted tests 1 and 2 red (the two comparing guide against emitted keys) and tests 3 and 4 green; measured 2 fail 2 pass. M2, delete contractVersion from the EMITTED envelope with the guide untouched: predicted ONLY test 1 red, failing on its explicit guard; measured 1 fail 3 pass, failing exactly on the guard line. M2 is the one that matters: it proves the test reads the CLIs real output rather than asserting the guide against the source constant, which would only prove the file agrees with itself.

CONFINEMENT: quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude exits 0 at state version-only with skill state current, so the managed CLAUDE.md block is byte-identical and unaffected by the guide change. The guide (guides.ts) and the managed block (agent-instructions.ts) are separate generators; this confirms that rather than assuming it.
finalSummary:
The overview guide now names the success envelope exactly as the CLI emits it, distinguishes success from error, says the record lives under data, and states the additive-key rule. Pinned by a test that compares the guide against real CLI output.

WHAT WAS WRONG. guides.ts stated: Every command supports --json (the {schemaVersion, kind, data, principal} envelope). The built CLI emits {schemaVersion, contractVersion, kind, data, principal} on success and {error_type, message, principal} on error. So the key list omitted contractVersion (QCLI-289, fixed at index 1 by the shared contract) and the singular word envelope concealed that success and error are two shapes sharing no payload key. Not a contract change: the envelopes were correct, their documentation was stale.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. This repositorys CLAUDE.md requires every agent to run quest instructions overview before answering or acting, so this is the highest-traffic sentence quest ships, and it is read immediately before a caller writes a jq path. An incomplete key list is the wrong input at exactly that moment.

THE SECOND DRIFT, found by the test rather than by me. Asserting the guide against every key task list actually emits failed on scope, DEC-6s additive key, which the guide also never mentioned. The list was short by two keys and the second was invisible to the inspection that found the first. So the fix states the RULE rather than an enumeration that cannot stay complete: some commands add a key between data and principal, principal is always last, and a caller must tolerate an unrecognized top-level key rather than treating the envelope as malformed -- which is the settled contract amendment, so the guide now teaches the tolerance the contract requires.

ALSO ADDED, from the reporting sessions own instance: if a projection comes back all-null, print the key set before concluding anything about the record. Their case was a uniform null across four fields from querying the top level instead of .data, which reads as a failed write rather than a wrong path; they nearly re-filed a task that existed, which on this tracker mints a duplicate id.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED. bun run check exits 0, 585 pass 0 fail. Four new tests spawn the real CLI: they compare the guide against the emitted success keys (using overview, the command with no additive key, so the fixed set and the rule are two separate claims), against the emitted error keys, against task lists real scope key and its position between data and principal, and assert the top-level projection really does miss while .data.id resolves.

MUTATION PROOF IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, since the test compares two artifacts and either could drift. M1, guide reverted with code untouched: predicted tests 1 and 2 red, 3 and 4 green; measured exactly that. M2, contractVersion deleted from the EMITTED envelope with the guide untouched: predicted ONLY test 1 red on its explicit guard; measured exactly that, failing on the guard line. M2 is the load-bearing one -- it proves the test reads real CLI output rather than asserting the guide against the source constant, which would only prove the file agrees with itself.

CONFINEMENT. quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude exits 0 at state version-only with skill state current, so the managed CLAUDE.md block is byte-identical; the guide and the managed block are separate generators and this confirms it rather than assuming it.
